sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: To express possession, Hungarian commonly uses a possessed noun with a dative possessor and van/vannak.

Nekünk ('to us') is the dative form behind miénk ('ours') — the two are built from the same root. When a possessive pronoun looks vaguely like a dative pronoun you already know, that's not a coincidence; they share the same person markers throughout the language.
